title: The Gadarene demoniac and the 'appointed time'

tellings.quote: Jesus was in in the land of Gdara with his disciples
they would chain him up in the tombs because he would scream.
tellings.difference: Adds the detail that he was chained in the tombs and screamed, and credits the New Testament instead of Jesus.
tellings.link_reason: Both tell the Gospel encounter with the Gadarene demoniac in the land of Gadara, and the teller is the same.

as_told.title: Gadarene demoniac chained in the tombs

tellings.quote: And the spirits of the giants =afflict=, oppress, destroy, attack, do battle, and work destruction on the earth, and cause trouble: they take no food, ⌜but nevertheless hunger⌝ and thirst, and cause offences.

From the days of the slaughter and destruction and death ⌜of the giants⌝, from the souls of whose flesh the spirits, having gone forth, shall destroy without incurring judgement—thus shall they destroy until the day of the consummation, the great ⌜judgement⌝ in which the age shall be consummated over the Watchers and the godless, yea, shall be wholly consummated.”

Ye †mighty kings† who dwell on the earth, ye shall have to behold Mine Elect One, how he sits on the throne of glory and judges Azâzêl, and all his associates, and all his hosts in the name of the Lord of Spirits.’

plain: A researcher named Tim Alberino tells Michels that the man possessed by demons whom Jesus met in the land of Gadara, a story from the New Testament, ties into the much older account of giants and their spirits, and the time set for their judgement. Alberino tells it from the scriptures without naming another source: Jesus was in Gadara with his disciples, and the people there would chain the man up in the tombs "because he would scream." He reads it alongside the Book of Enoch, an ancient Jewish text left out of most Bibles, quoted here in R. H. Charles's 1917 translation. Enoch says that "the spirits of the giants afflict, oppress, destroy, attack, do battle, and work destruction on the earth", and that they will go on destroying "until the day of the consummation, the great judgement" over the Watchers, the fallen angels who fathered them. Elsewhere Enoch has kings "behold Mine Elect One" on the throne of glory judging Azazel, a leader of the fallen angels, "and all his hosts." Set side by side, both texts tell of tormenting spirits loose on the earth until a fixed day of judgement; the link between the two is Alberino's reading. If he is right, the demons of the Gospels would be the spirits of the ancient giants.
